bull.b: Data center now represents the majority of revenue and management projects sustained ~50% annual growth. Durable design wins and large-scale customer ramps in servers, switches, and optics anchor multi-year revenue visibility and create high‑stickiness OEM relationships that support predictable volume growth.

High margins and sizeable OCF/FCF provide durable internal funding for R&D, capacity prepayments, and M&A without immediate reliance on external financing. Persistent cash generation enhances flexibility to support product ramps, customer financing needs, and capital returns while insulating operations across the cycle.

Partnerships with tier‑one customers and targeted M&A deepen differentiated IP across photonics, optics, and custom XPU-related silicon. These moves improve technology roadmaps, shorten time‑to‑market for advanced interconnects, and strengthen competitive barriers in high‑growth infrastructure segments.

bear.b: A large portion of forecast growth assumes persistent, elevated cloud and AI capital spending. Should hyperscaler CapEx moderate or shift architectures, Marvell's multi‑year ramps and revenue trajectory would be vulnerable, creating material downside to near‑term and multi‑year revenue visibility.

bear.t: Higher leverage and dilution from deals
bear.b: Acquisition-related debt and increased share count raise interest expense and shareholder dilution risk. Elevated leverage reduces financial flexibility for opportunistic investments or cyclical downturns, and higher shares can magnify the impact of any revenue or margin shortfalls on per‑share metrics.

bear.t: Execution and timing risk on ambitious ramps
bear.b: Targets like large custom/XPU adoption and scale‑up optics require multi‑year development and customer validation. Delays or slower adoption would compress expected margin expansion and cash returns, making projected revenue milestones and associated investments sensitive to execution timing.
